newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent steady, support on squaring before API.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent steady, support on squaring before API.

text.p: Brent crude futures were untraded in late afternoon dealings on Tuesday and shying away from setting a one-year low for Brent front-month crude.
July Brent was quoted on SIMEX at $17.56/$17.60 per barrel after earlier being bid as low as $17.45.
London settled at $17.56 per barrel overnight for a loss of 14 cents on the day, but tested key support at $17.54, the lowest price since April 10.
A break below $17.54 would take prices to their lowest level since June 14, 1996.
NYMEX July futures were three cents down on ACCESS after New York dropped 11 cents to $18.68 after hitting a fresh 16 month low of $18.60.
July NYMEX was last traded on ACCESS at $18.65 per barrel after falling in New York ACCESS trade to $18.55.
Brokers said the market could find support as players square positions ahead of the API data due later from the U.S.
"We should be able to hold these levels ahead of the APIs," one broker said.
